text: Théodore Gardelle (30 November 1722 – 4 April 1761) was a painter and enameller. He was born in Geneva, which was then part of the independent Republic of Geneva, where he began studying portrait miniature painting. After gaining the basic skills, he moved to Paris in 1744, where he developed significant proficiency in painting. He resided in Paris, studying and painting until 1750. Following this, he returned to Geneva, where he continued practicing his profession for several years. In 1756, he went back to Paris. In 1760, he traveled to England, where he was executed in Haymarket, London, for murdering his landlady Anne King.
